content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passes all quality checks. Per our Spec-Driven workflow, **this is a review gate** — nothing gets planned or built until you approve the spec.

## 📄 Specification ready for your review

**Files**
- Spec: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- Quality checklist: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` (all items pass ✅)

### What the spec proposes — in plain terms

**Three prioritized slices** (each usable on its own):

| Priority | User story | The gist |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| **P1** | Save a bookmark | Paste an address (optional title/notes), it's validated and saved to your list |
| **P2** | Browse, search & open | See your list, filter by keyword as you type, click to open the page in a new tab |
| **P3** | Edit & delete | Fix titles/addresses, remove items with a confirmation step |

**Also included:** tags/labels for grouping and filtering, duplicate-address warnings, an empty/first-run state, and persistence so bookmarks survive closing and reopening.

### Key scope decisions I made (please confirm)

These were the judgment calls — I picked sensible defaults and documented them as **Assumptions** rather than blocking on questions:

1. **Single user, single device, no login** for v1 — no accounts or cross-device sync.
2. **Web app** (usable on a phone browser), no native mobile app.
3. **No automatic page-title/favicon fetching** — titles come from you or are derived from the address. Flagged as a possible future enhancement.

### Your options at this gate

- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan) for your next review.
- ✏️ **Request changes** → tell me what's wrong or missing and I'll update the spec.
- ❓ **Want the ambiguities probed more formally?** → I can run `speckit-clarify` first.

A few things worth a decision from you:
- Are the three scope assumptions above right, especially **single-device / no sync**?
- Do you want **tags** in v1 (currently in), or defer them?
- Is **fetching the real page title automatically** something you'd want (currently deferred)?

How would you like to proceed?

Please revise the spec before planning:

- Single-user, single-device with no login or sync is fine for v1.
- Keep tags in v1.
- When I save a link, I want the app to automatically collect its real title, description, favicon, and preview image. I should still be able to edit the title and description.
- If I save an address that already exists, take me to edit the existing bookmark instead of merely warning me.

The spec is revised and still passes the quality checklist. Back at the review gate.

## 📄 Spec updated — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

Here's what changed against your four points:

| Your request | How the spec now reads |
|---|---|
| Single-user, single-device, no login/sync for v1 | ✅ Kept as-is (Assumption #1) |
| Keep tags in v1 | ✅ Kept (FR-014, Tag entity) |
| Auto-collect real title, description, favicon, preview on save; still edit title & description | ✅ **FR-004** (fetch all four), **FR-004a** (edit title/description), **FR-004b** (graceful fallback if fetch fails/times out). User no longer types a title; notes stay user-authored |
| Duplicate address → open the existing bookmark to edit | ✅ **FR-011** now routes to editing the existing bookmark instead of just warning |

**Other ripples I handled so the spec stays consistent:**
- Save flow (User Story 1) rewritten around auto-fetch, with an explicit fallback scenario.
- Bookmark entity gained `description`, `favicon`, `preview image` (title/description marked auto-fetched + user-editable).
- Assumption reversed: metadata fetching is now **in scope**, noting it requires outbound internet access and a bounded fetch timeout.
- Added **SC-006** (real title + preview appear with no manual entry) and **SC-007** (saving never hangs on a slow/unreachable page).

### One thing worth your call before we plan

Auto-fetching introduces a small behavior question: **should saving feel instant, or wait for the fetch?**
- **A — Save instantly, enrich in the background:** bookmark appears immediately, then title/preview fill in a moment later. Feels fast.
- **B — Wait for the fetch (with timeout), then show the finished bookmark:** slightly slower save, but the item is complete when it appears.

The spec currently allows either (it just requires saving never hangs). If you have a preference I'll pin it down; otherwise I'll leave it as an implementation choice for the plan.

**Approve the revised spec to move to `speckit-plan`?** Or tell me to adjust anything (including A vs. B above).

Choose A: save immediately and fill in the page details in the background, with a clear fallback if fetching fails. With that pinned down, I approve the revised specification. Please proceed to the implementation plan.

## 🧭 Implementation plan ready for review — plan gate

**Artifacts written to `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`:**
- `plan.md` — the implementation plan
- `research.md` — technical decisions (Phase 0)
- `data-model.md` — Bookmark/Tag entities + storage schema
- `contracts/api.md` — the JSON API contract
- `quickstart.md` — run + validation guide

### The plan in plain terms

**Shape:** One small Node.js web app that both serves the browser UI and answers a JSON API — no separate frontend build, no external services. Everything runs in a single process on port 4000.

**How your requirements map to the design:**

| Your requirement | Plan approach |
|---|---|
| Save immediately, fill details in background (choice A) | On save, the bookmark is stored and shown instantly with a URL-based title and a "fetching…" state; the server fetches the page's real title/description/favicon/preview **in the background** and the item updates in place |
| Real metadata collected automatically | Server fetches the page (browsers can't, due to cross-site restrictions) and reads standard Open Graph / meta tags |
| Still edit title & description | Edit endpoint allows overriding both |
| Clear fallback if fetching fails | 8-second timeout; on failure the bookmark stays, marked "failed", keeping a URL-derived title + placeholder — saving never hangs |
| Duplicate address → edit existing | Save detects an existing match and opens that bookmark's edit view instead of duplicating |
| Tags in v1 | Tag/label model + filter |
| Single-user, single-device, no login | Local SQLite file for storage; no accounts/sync |

**Persistence:** a local database file, so bookmarks survive restarts.

**Key technical choices (yours to veto):**
- **Runtime/stack:** Node.js + Express, plain HTML/CSS/JS frontend (no React), SQLite file for storage, `cheerio` to parse page metadata.
- **Background enrichment** via a simple in-process async task (no job-queue infrastructure — overkill for one user).
- **Testing:** Node's built-in test runner for unit/API + Playwright for one end-to-end run.

**One thing I decided that's worth confirming:** favicon and preview image are stored as **links to the original image URLs**, not downloaded copies. Simpler, and fine unless you want offline previews if the source disappears — say the word and I'll add image caching to the spec/plan.

### Your options at this gate
- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-tasks` (the dependency-ordered task breakdown), then `speckit-implement`.
- ✏️ **Change something** — stack, background-vs-queue, image caching, or anything above.

Shall I generate the task breakdown?

I approve the plan. Linking to the original favicon and preview images is fine for this version; offline image caching isn’t necessary. Please generate the task breakdown and proceed with implementation.

## ✅ Bookmark Manager — implemented and verified

I built the app end-to-end against the approved spec, plan, and tasks. Everything was driven through the SDD gates — no ad-hoc coding.

### What works (all validated)
- **Save is instant, details fill in the background (choice A):** posting a URL returns immediately with a URL-derived title and a "fetching details…" state; the server then fetches the real title/description/favicon/preview and the card updates in place. Verified live against `example.com` — title enriched to "Example Domain".
- **Graceful fallback:** unreachable/non-HTML pages settle to a "preview unavailable" state, keeping the URL-derived title. Saving never hangs (8s timeout, off the request path).
- **Invalid address rejected** with an actionable inline message; **duplicate address opens the existing bookmark to edit** (not just a warning).
- **Browse, keyword search (title/url/description), tag filter, open-in-new-tab, empty/no-results states.**
- **Edit** (title, description, address, notes, tags) and **delete with confirmation**; edits persist across restart (SQLite file).

### Test results
- **Unit + integration:** 18/18 passing (`npm test`) — offline, injected metadata fetcher.
- **End-to-end:** Playwright happy path passing (`npm run test:e2e`) — save → appears → enrichment fills in → search → edit → delete.
- **Live smoke test:** real server on `0.0.0.0`, real metadata fetch, duplicate → 409, all confirmed.

### How to run
```bash
npm install
npm start        # http://maker:4000
```

### Ready for your review
`/work/.harness/app.json` is written (`kind: application`, port 4000, `npm start`), and the UI sets `data-harness-ready="true"` after the initial list loads. The broker will start the server for the review container — open **http://maker:4000**.

**Artifacts:** spec, plan, research, data-model, contract, quickstart, and tasks (29/29 ✅) are all in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`. Source in `src/` + `public/`, tests in `tests/`.

One note for a possible future iteration (already flagged in the spec as out of scope for v1): favicons/previews are stored as links to the original images, and there's no login/sync — single device only. Want me to demo any specific flow, or shall we call this version done?
